# Host CLI lifecycle: versions visible, minimum version per model, host-owned upgrade with drain, drift alarm

Operator decision 2026-09-12. Driving case: on 2026-09-12 the fleet could not use gpt-6-astra because agent-runner-01 runs codex-cli 0.144.1 (astra needs 0.153 or newer, current 0.154.0) and claude-code 2.1.202 (current 2.1.269). The product showed the model as "Not offered by codex-cli 0.144.1" (AGT-2707) but offered no way to fix it and did not say why; the operator upgraded by hand as root over SSH. A third party installing the product hits the same wall at the first provider model change. Today the agent CLIs are installed by docs/operations/setup/linux-runner-host.md and scripts/remote-runner-onboard.sh with an unpinned `npm i -g`, and the runner's sudo allowlist (agent-runner-deploy) has no upgrade command.

## Deliver

1. **Versions in the capability snapshot.** Every host reports the installed CLIs with name, version, install path and the timestamp of the check; Execution Hosts shows them per host with the age of the check. The remote runner and the review daemon collect this the same way.

Failure leaves the previous version in place (npm install of a pinned version into a staging prefix, swap on success).

# A coding run can saturate the shared runner host; the runner must bound what one run may consume

## Finding (17.09.2026, agent-runner-01 = 12 cores shared by 2 coding slots and 2 review slots, operator evidence)

Three times today an Opus coding run, asked to reproduce a flaky test "under contention", started CPU busy loops on the host and drove the load average far past the core count while other work ran:

| Time | Card | What ran | Load (1 min) | Collateral |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 14:09-14:27 | AGT-2859 | `/tmp/stress.sh 24` = 24 `while :; do :; done` loops | 76 | AGT-2858 review suite and AGT-2860 coding run slowed; review flaked |
| 21:30-21:35 | AGT-2864 | 49 `bash -c while :; do :; done` | 35 | develop->main promotion gate running in parallel |
| 21:45-22:05 | AGT-2864 | 24, then 104 busy loops | 41 | host otherwise idle |

Each time the operator killed the loops by hand (`pkill -f 'while :[;] do :[;] done'`); the runs continued unharmed and delivered. Nothing in the runner limits a detached coding worker's process tree: no CPU quota, no nice level, no child-process count, no load-based throttle for the run itself (the load-aware admission in `RUNNER_CLAIM_MAX_LOAD_PER_CORE` only delays new claims). A single run can therefore degrade every other slot on the host and, through the review executor, turn healthy reviews into timing failures.

## Deliver

1. Resource envelope per detached worker: run each coding worker (and each review worker) in its own cgroup with a CPU weight/quota derived from the slot count (for example `cpu.max` = `cores / (codingSlots + reviewSlots)` with burst, and `cpu.weight` so reviews are not starved by coding), plus a `pids.max` cap sized for a build/test tree (dotnet + node + shells, a few hundred), so a runaway agent cannot fork hundreds of loops. Use systemd transient scopes (`systemd-run --scope -p CPUQuota=... -p TasksMax=...`) or the cgroup v2 API directly; document the chosen mechanism and how it survives the KillMode=process / PrivateTmp=no decisions of AGT-2750.
2. Visibility: the runner logs the worker's CPU seconds and peak tasks at the end of a run and reports them in the delivery (`results/status.md` block or the run summary), so a card that needed 2,000 CPU seconds is distinguishable from one that spun.
3. Load-aware backpressure for a running run is out of scope; the envelope is the mechanism. But

# A Task Server restart during the pre-develop gate leaves the un-gated merge on the integration branch and marks the card integrated

## Symptom (16.09.2026, Stable v0.4.0 rollout, three restarts at 13:07, 13:17 and 13:47)
Each restart hit a running pre-develop build gate (AGT-2703 at 13:06, AGT-2816 at 13:18, AGT-2794 at 13:33). The gate process died with the backend, no rollback ran, and the merge commit stayed on the integration branch: the Studio-owned integration worktree (`%TEMP%\agent-studio-integration\agent-taskboard-dev-7cad6883`) sits at `db4afad43` = origin/develop 3d4168c80 + `831aff3cf` (AGT-2703, never gated) + `0af3306bc` (AGT-2816, never gated) + `db4afad43` (AGT-2843, gate running). The next integrations were merged on top of the un-gated ones, so a later gate tests and, on success, pushes all of them together; on failure the rollback returns only to the previous un-gated tip. Meanwhile AGT-2703 and AGT-2816 show `integration.status=integrated, detail=anchor-ancestor` on the card although neither commit is on origin/develop, and AGT-2794 shows `pending` with nothing scheduled to resume its integration.

## Expected
- A gate that does not reach a verdict (process gone, restart, timeout of the host) is recorded as an interrupted run, and startup recovery either rolls the integration branch back to the pre-merge tip or re-runs the gate for that exact merge before anything else is merged on top. Un-gated merges never accumulate on the integration branch.
- `integration.status=integrated` requires the delivery to be reachable from the pushed remote integration branch (origin/develop); a delivery reachable only from a local or worktree branch is `merged-locally` (or `pending`) with that detail, and the card timeline says which.
- A card whose integration was interrupted is re-queued for integration automatically after restart (sequence resumes), without a new remote review when the review verdict is still valid for the same SHA.
- Tests: restart harness in backend.Tests that kills a fake gate mid-run, restarts the runner service and asserts rollback-or-resume plus the projection; projection test for local-only ancestry. Related: AGT-2780 (restart contract), AGT-2824 (integration retry without new review), AGT-2832 (integration worktree), AGT-2838 (stale integration state).

## Working rules
- Base on current origin/develop. Keep the change focus

# Completed-push backstop: push only the integrated result, stop retrying superseded run commits

## Context (operator finding 2026-09-07)

- `CompletedPushBackstopHostedService` runs every 15 minutes over every completed card and calls `PushCompletedJobCommitsAsync`, which pushes each entry of `task.json commits[]` to the project's main branch (`GitService.PushShaAsync`).
- QS-85 (Quality Studio) completed with 42 attributed commits from 73 fences; only the two commits of the final, integrated fence are ancestors of `origin/main`. The other 40 are superseded intermediate commits. The backstop pushes all 40 every cycle, GitHub rejects each as non-fast-forward, and the backend logs `Auto-push skipped … remote-rejected … ! [rejected] <sha> -> main (non-fast-forward)`: 4,009 such lines and as many GitHub pushes on 2026-09-07 alone, plus one `managed-repo-push-failure` bus event per attempt. The card's integration is `integrated` (anchor-ancestor), so nothing is missing; the loop is pure waste and hides real push failures in the log.

## Changes

1. Push selection: for a completed card the backstop pushes only commits that are reachable from the card's integrated result (`integration.sha` or the reviewed result SHA) and not yet on the remote main; commits that are neither ancestors of the integrated result nor of the remote main are marked `superseded` in the commit record and skipped permanently.
2. Backoff and terminal state: a commit rejected as non-fast-forward is retried with exponential backoff (15 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h) and after the fourth rejection recorded as `push-rejected` with the git error; the backstop no longer touches it. The card shows the state in the integration panel, and a single bus event is emitted when the state changes, not per attempt.
3. Skip integrated cards: when `integration.status == integrated` and the integrated SHA is on the remote main, the backstop skips the card entirely.
4. Log discipline: one summary line per backstop cycle (cards scanned, pushed, skipped-superseded, rejected) instead of a warning per commit.
5. Tests: unit tests for the selection rule (integrated ancestor pushed, superseded skipped, remote-rejected backoff and terminal state), a backstop cycle test with a fake git service that counts push calls (one push per pending commit, zero for an integrated card), and a log assertion for the summary line.

## Acceptan

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent-studio | 2,410 | 1,125 | 982 | 160 | 119 | ~20 |
| quality-studio | 2,579 | 1,212 | 1,207 | 144 | 2 | ~10 |
| token-economy | 117 | 52 | 50 | 9 | 2 | 2 |

On agent-studio 1,024 of these refs already have their tip contained in `origin/main` (525 results, 407 salvage, 86 runner, 6 quarantine); 529 results and 384 salvage refs are older than 30 days.

The whole board sat in Human Review and nothing could be accepted. The cause was

itself, so the review step `verify-5` exited 1 for every delivery, every remote
review graded `ProductFailure`, and the acceptance rail refused each card with
"Remote Review ended with 'ProductFailure', not Pass". Deliveries then piled up
and were integrated by hand instead, which is how the operator merges of the
last weeks happened.

The failing step is `lint:components`
(`frontend/scripts/check-component-size.mjs`). Its baseline file
`frontend/scripts/component-size-baseline.json` was last written on 2026-08-19
and eight components had grown past it since, with no baseline row at all for
three of them:

| `app.ts` | total 5477 to 5626 |
| `overview-pane.component.ts` | total 4336 to 4366 |
| `explorer-workspace-tree.component.ts` | total 931 to 937 |

"Das Zielbild sollte sein, dass der Remote-Host auch merged. Der lokale Studio soll nur schauen."

```
## Symptom

The user has emphasised repeatedly that visual feedback (Playwright screenshots, captured images, before/after comparisons) is *the* primary signal that something actually shipped. Today the rendered task documents rarely show those screenshots, and when they do appear they are not clickable - the user cannot open the full image, cannot scrub through a sequence, cannot tell whether the Playwright run that produced them passed or failed.

## Goal

Screenshots become the loudest line in the task review surface. The workspace-level activity feed gains a "visual feedback" lane that aggregates the latest screenshots across all projects.

## Deliverables

1. **Per-task surface**:

   - Click a thumbnail to open a lightbox: full-size image, prev/next navigation, optional pass/fail badge, and a "open in Explorer" link to the file on disk.
   - The strip is populated from `<job>/results/*.png` and from `frontend/test-results/**/*.png` when the spec was billable for the job.
   - When no screenshots exist, the strip is hidden (no placeholder takes space).

4. **Tests**:
```

```
# Project Wiki + Common-Problems-Library als First-Class-Citizen

## Motivation
Operator (2026-05-27): "Wir haben ja immer wieder diese genauen Probleme und Bugs. Lass uns mal eine Library erstellen, wo die aktuellen Probleme und Bugs immer wieder auftreten. First-Class Citizen auf Projektebene, wo ich Common-Problems sammle und ordne."

Heute (innerhalb von 24h) sind diese Probleme MEHRFACH aufgetreten und kosten jedes Mal Diagnose-Zeit:

| Problem | Erscheinung | Anzahl Vorkommen heute |
|---|---|---|
| EACCES (POSIX permission denied) | Claude-CLI kann file nicht schreiben (z.B. JobMutationService.cs) | mind. 1, in mehreren Jobs |
| Claude-Code tool permission denied | "Permission denied and could not request permission from user" | mind. 2 Runs |
| Circuit-breaker 3x consecutive failure | mode auto-continuous -> manual | 10x heute |
| Stale-progress orphan race | job-folder verschwindet mid-pickup -> orphan-<slug>-<date> | min. 3x |
| Copilot CLI exit=1 nach 0.0s | Copilot scheitert sofort, picked aber im Round-Robin | min. 7x |
| Project filter name divergenz | Agent Task Processor (WatchPath) vs Agent Software Studio (Registry) | dauerhaft |
| Workspace-Create unsichtbar | persistiert auf disk, fehlt im /api/registry/workspaces | 1x sichtbar |
| Job-Card zeigt "human" statt Modell | agent-Field-Leak | bei jedem neuen Job |
| Direkt-Schreibzugriff auf Workspace-Folders | Agent (ich) schrieb mehrfach mit Write statt API | 2x in einer Session |

Jedes mal "neu" diagnostizieren ist nicht haltbar. Wir brauchen ein **First-Class-Wissens-Lager** im Repo, das ein Agent (und ein Operator) ZUERST konsultiert, wenn ein Symptom auftaucht, und das systematisch befuellt wird mit jedem neuen Vorkommen.

## Konzept

### Ablage-Struktur
Neu unter `docs/wiki/` (alternative: `wiki/` als Top-Level-Ordner — fuer Diskussion). Innerhalb:

```
docs/wiki/
  README.md                                     # Index + Suche-Anleitung + Konventionen
  common-problems/
    README.md                                   # Index aller bekannten Probleme + Tag-Cloud + Status
    eacces-on-dev-file-writes/
      README.md                                 # Exec-Summary: was, wann zuerst, Status (open/mitigated/fixed)
      occurrences.md                            # Timeline jedes Vorkommens (UTC, Job-ID, Agent, betroffener Pfad)
      protocol.md                               # Detail-Root-C

# Task Server principals: separate Studio, Engine, and per-Runner credentials with scopes, revocation, and hub auth

## Context (operator decision 2026-09-06)

- Phase B (docs/operations/remote-task-server-local-studio.md) is approved; slice B2. The packaged install defaults to one shared bearer (`AUTH=bearer`, one service credential) and an interim profile with `StudioBearerToken` and `RunnerBearerToken`. The plan's release gates require: missing or invalid auth returns 401, insufficient scope returns 403, `X-Client-Id` alone never authorizes, and a compromised-Runner simulation cannot call Studio or management mutations.
- No API listener may open on the private network (D2) until these negative tests pass, so this card gates the remote deployment.
- Code: task-server/TaskServerAuthenticationMiddleware.cs, TaskServerOptions.cs, TaskServerBootstrapOptions.cs, TaskServerEndpoints.cs, TaskServerProtocolMiddleware.cs; studio-bff reads `TaskServer:AuthTokenFile`; runner reads `RUNNER_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE`; engine reads engine.env.

## Changes

1. Principal model: credentials are stored hash-only in the Task Server store with `principalId`, `kind` (studio, engine, runner), `scopes`, `createdAt`, `revokedAt`, `lastSeenAt`. Runners get one credential each (`runnerId` bound). Bootstrap creates the initial Studio and Engine credentials and prints them once; management endpoints under `/api/v1/management/principals` create, list, rotate, and revoke (rotation keeps the old secret valid for a configurable overlap).
2. Route scopes: every v1 route and hub declares its required scope (`tasks:read`, `tasks:write`, `runs:claim`, `reviews:claim`, `management`, `events:subscribe`, …). 2. "When I then press Back in the browser, I want to get to the previous task: a browser feature."

1. `Task total SUM` (`overview-pane.component.html`, `pipelineTotal()`) is the token and cost sum of the pipeline steps of the **currently shown pipeline execution only** (`pipelinePoll.pipeline()?.cost`), i.e. the latest run plus its pre, post and review steps. `Tokens across all runs` is the sum over every run of the card. Nothing on screen says so; "Task total" reads as the larger of the two and is the smaller ($3.15 against $28.88).
2. The value `2m` is a token count: `formatTokens` in `overview-pane-formatters.ts` renders 2,000,000 as `2m` (lower-case `m`, `.0` stripped), directly beside durations like `7m 29s` and `15m` that use the same letter for minutes, while the neighbouring block renders `41.65M`. It reads as "two minutes".
3. The pipeline groups expand with a `+` at the left edge; the run rows and `Tokens across all runs` expand with a `>` chevron that sits further right. Two expander styles, two columns.
4. `Agent Work` (`overview-agent-work.component.html`): `Calls` is the number of CLI invocations (sessions) of the card, here identical to the four runs listed directly above; the two timestamps are first start and last touch without column headers; the token and cost cells are hard-coded `-`. The `Tools` row and the drill-down only render when `toolCalls > 0`, which is never the case for remote runs on this installation, so the block shows one row of mostly dashes.

## Deli
